narrations.en: Step 16 (Final Step): The visual proof is complete! Starting from the starting condition of applying a linear transformation that changes a12, the x component of the two-column basis vector e2(0,1) of the matrix, to the unit square area of the coordinate plane, which was the starting condition, instead of manually inserting countless points inside the area, the horizontal reference arrow e1=(1,0) and the vertical reference arrow e2=(0,1) go through the base arrow auxiliary line that tracks which coordinates the two basis vectors move to, and then the matrix components. It was clearly confirmed that, according to the value of a12, the x component of the two-column basis vector e2(0,1), a geometric transformation law is established in which a unit square lattice performs a horizontal shear transformation (Cavalieri equivalent transformation) that creates a parallelogram by pushing the upper side of the shape diagonally in the horizontal direction while maintaining the vertical height. The key point to remember here is that if you try to solve a linear transformation problem only by substituting complex simultaneous equations, it is easy to get lost! Always observe first as a geometric basis shift that (1,0) moves to the first column and (0,1) moves to the second column. Finally, ask a deeper question. If the two column vectors of the matrix lie on a straight line and the parallelogram is distorted into flat line segments (determinant a11a22 - a12a21 = 0), why can't there be an inverse transformation (inverse matrix)?
